assertions.A1_engine_canonicalizes: passed — 'Nazgul' and 'Nazgûl' both resolve to canonical deck-count key 'nazgûl' against the pinned v0.85.0 card-data.json (replicating the engine's lookup_key + fold_card_name_key + face-name algorithm); canonical bucket = 18 > printed-override ceiling 9, so the engine's copy_limit_violations flags the 9+9 deck. Confirms the issue's scoping: no illegal playable deck can result; the bug is stale-affordance only.
assertions.A2_gap1_alias_counted_separately: passed — after text-importing 5x 'Nazgul' + 4x 'Nazgûl' (canonical total 9 = ceiling), the real hook reports canIncrement true for BOTH spellings, and handleIncrementCard('Nazgul') climbs 5 -> 6 (canonical 10 > 9). The '+' affordance stays live past the real ceiling.
assertions.A3_gap2_searchadd_ungated: passed — four handleAddCard('Lightning Bolt') then canIncrement is false (limits landed), but a fifth handleAddCard walks the count 4 -> 5. The search-result add path ignores the copy limit.
assertions.A4_control_plus_gated: passed — handleIncrementCard('Lightning Bolt') at 5 copies is a no-op (the #6654-gated '+' control works); the walk-past is specific to the search-add path.

The mock returns the same ceiling for both spellings because the real engine canonicalizes the name BEFORE resolving the ceiling (deck_validation.rs max_deck_copies: 'let canonical = canonical_deck_count_key(db, name);').

driver_notes: Engine code paths grounding the mock + the canonicalization leg: deck_validation.rs::canonical_deck_count_key ('Uses the indexed face name when the card resolves so alias spellings ("Nazgul" vs "Nazgûl") merge into one bucket for copy-limit checks.'); max_deck_copies canonicalizes before resolving ('let canonical = canonical_deck_count_key(db, name);'); combined_copy_counts keys the map by canonical_deck_count_key; copy_limit_violations runs over those canonical counts. Client paths: useDeckBuilder.ts combinedCopyCounts (useMemo, keys by entry.name raw); canIncrement reads combinedCopyCounts.get(name); handleIncrementCard gates on canIncrement (the #6654 control); handleAddCard has no canIncrement reference.

Browser UI not exercised; the search-results component's disabled-state shape (the issue's proposed fix direction) is a design decision, not asserted.
result: Both reported gaps reproduce on current mainline (12a8ef4). Gap 1: the client's combinedCopyCounts keys by raw entry name, so a text-imported deck with 5x 'Nazgul' + 4x 'Nazgûl' (canonical 9/9) leaves canIncrement true for both spellings and the '+' climbs to a canonical 10. Gap 2: handleAddCard increments past the ceiling (Lightning Bolt 4 -> 5) while canIncrement is false; the '+' control itself is correctly gated (control). Engine-side check confirms the issue's scoping: the engine canonicalizes both spellings to one bucket (18 > 9 ceiling), so copy_limit_violations still rejects the deck — stale affordance, not a legality hole.
scope: Deck-builder subsystem (area:engine + area:deckbuilder): the client copy-limit affordance in useDeckBuilder.ts. Gap 1 = combinedCopyCounts keys by raw entry name (no canonicalization). Gap 2 = handleAddCard (search-result add path) never consults canIncrement. Native engine / browser game-state pair N/A; equivalent observable contract defined in the deckbuilder subsystem per playbook step 2.
